title: Coefficient transposition and field descent of the five-arrow Hom chain
statement:
Fix the finite-field, finite-type scheme and four coefficient-stage conventions of [def-fix-six-functor-datum], and a separated finite-type $f:X\to Y$ exceptionally admissible in the sense of [def-weil-exceptional-adjoint-admissibility]. For finite or integral $\Lambda$, let $M\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ and $N,L\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$. Put $H=R\mathcal Hom$, $A=Rf_*H_X(M,f^!N)$ and $B=H_Y(Rf_!M,N)$. Use the specified adjunctions of [fix-prop-adjunctions] and the specified compact-support projection $\operatorname{PF}_{f,M,L}:Rf_!M\otimes^LL\to Rf_!(M\otimes^LLf^*L)$ of [def-exchange-projection]. Integral tensors are completed. Suppose the following five adjunction/projection bijections are defined on the indicated full domains, and denote their composite by $\Gamma_{M,N,L}$:
$$\operatorname{Hom}_Y(L,A)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_X(Lf^*L,H_X(M,f^!N))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_X(M\otimes^LLf^*L,f^!N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Y(Rf_!(M\otimes^LLf^*L),N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Y(Rf_!M\otimes^LL,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Y(L,B).$$
The fourth arrow is precomposition with $\operatorname{PF}_{f,M,L}$, and all transposes use the canonical evaluations, units and counits.

Let $T$ be finite quotient reduction $A_{E,n}\to A_{E,m}$, $n\geq m\geq1$, integral reduction $R\to A_{E,n}$, or integral scalar extension $\mathcal O_E\to\mathcal O_F$ for a finite coefficient-field extension $E\subset F$. For the specified coefficient comparisons of the operations, write $\alpha_A:T(A)\xrightarrow{\sim}A'$ and $\alpha_B:T(B)\xrightarrow{\sim}B'$, where primes mean the same formulas on the changed inputs. For every $u:L\to A$,
$$\alpha_B\circ T(\Gamma_{M,N,L}(u))=\Gamma_{TM,TN,TL}(\alpha_A\circ T(u)).$$
This is an equality of actual morphisms, is coherent under successive coefficient changes, and applies to all the stated finite-Tor inputs without a site-perfectness hypothesis.

Use raw rationalization [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] and the common-stage category [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], with the induced operations of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. The integral $\mathcal O_E$-linear bijections $\Gamma$ induce $E$-linear bijections on the localized Hom groups. If an inverse pair $a:B\to A$, $b:A\to B$ represents $\Gamma^{-1},\Gamma$ by postcomposition, its images remain inverse and represent these localized bijections. For algebraically closed coefficients, the same bijections and representing inverse maps, formed over any common finite coefficient field for the finitely many inputs, are independent of enlarging that field and of its representatives. Naturality, composition, coefficient-comparison and shift equations satisfied at the integral stages pass to these rational and common-stage maps.

proof.text: Fix a permitted coefficient change, writing $T_X,T_Y$ for its functors. All intermediate comparisons below are the specified ones, not arbitrary isomorphisms between their endpoints. The full-domain and comparison-isomorphism hypotheses in the statement are retained. The operation comparisons preserve tensor associators, evaluations, units and counits by [lem-fix-operation-reduction]. In the finite-quotient case we do not use that lemma's site-perfect internal-Hom invertibility assertion: use instead the canonical evaluation transpose $c_H:TH(K,Q)\to H(TK,TQ)$. Its transpose identity, naturality and compatibility with tensor-Hom transposition are [lem-coef-evaluation-transpose-coherence]; that statement expressly needs no invertibility of $c_H$. The specified internal-Hom comparisons are these evaluation transposes (for integral reduction this is also explicitly [lem-coef-integral-hom-reduction]). Consequently the calculation applies on the hypothesized domains, even when $M$ or $Rf_!M$ is not site-perfect. This argument proves compatibility of the comparisons; existence or invertibility outside those domains is not inferred.

source.place: Step 1 and final coefficient-comparison and field-stage sentences; explicit transposition and scalar-localization calculation

proof.text:
For the first arrow put $P=Lf^*$, $S=Rf_*$, $H=H_X(M,f^!N)$ and write $p:T_XP\xrightarrow{\sim}P'T_Y$, $s:T_YS\xrightarrow{\sim}S'T_X$. The inverse-adjunction transpose of $u:L\to SH$ is $q=\varepsilon_H\circ P(u)$. Counit compatibility gives
$$\varepsilon'_{T_XH}\circ P'(s_H)=T_X(\varepsilon_H)\circ p_{SH}^{-1}.$$
Naturality of $p$ therefore gives
$$\varepsilon'_{T_XH}\circ P'(s_H\circ T_Yu)=T_X(q)\circ p_L^{-1}.$$
These are the counit-mate identity [lem-amb-mate-unit-counit] for $p^{-1}$ and its specified mate $s$, with the comparison normalization of [lem-fix-operation-reduction]. Postcompose by the internal-Hom input comparison $T_XH\to H'_X(T_XM,f'^!T_YN)$; naturality of the adjunction then gives exactly the first coefficient square.

source.place: Step 1 and final coefficient-comparison and field-stage sentences; explicit transposition and scalar-localization calculation

proof.text:
The second arrow sends $q:PL\to H_X(M,f^!N)$ to
$$v=\operatorname{ev}_{M,f^!N}\circ(1_M\otimes q):M\otimes PL\to f^!N.$$
The evaluation-transpose identity of [lem-coef-evaluation-transpose-coherence], with the tensor symmetry when changing its displayed $T\otimes K$ order to our $K\otimes T$ order, says that the transpose of $c_H\circ T_Xq$ is $T_Xv$ precomposed with the canonical tensor comparison. Its symmetry compatibility is a hypothesis of that lemma and is part of the specified tensor comparisons. The completed tensor is used throughout at the integral stage, where the chain's completed adjunction is assumed. Finally compose with the comparisons for $PL$ and $f^!N$. Naturality in the two Hom variables gives the required second square. No dualizability or site-perfect replacement is made.

source.place: Step 1 and final coefficient-comparison and field-stage sentences; explicit transposition and scalar-localization calculation

proof.text:
Write $F=Rf_!$, $E=f^!$, with counit $\mu:FE\to1$, and set $Q=M\otimes PL$. The third arrow is $v\mapsto w=\mu_N\circ F(v)$. Let $c_F:T_YF\xrightarrow{\sim}F'T_X$ and $c_E:T_XE\xrightarrow{\sim}E'T_Y$ be the specified comparisons. The mate-counit identity is
$$\mu'_{T_YN}\circ F'(c_{E,N})=T_Y(\mu_N)\circ c_{F,EN}^{-1}.$$
Using naturality of $c_F$ gives
$$\mu'_{T_YN}\circ F'(c_{E,N}\circ T_Xv)=T_Y(w)\circ c_{F,Q}^{-1}.$$
This is [lem-amb-mate-unit-counit] applied to $F\dashv E$, $F'\dashv E'$ and $c_F^{-1}$; [lem-fix-operation-reduction] fixes the counit-compatible comparison, including the admissible exceptional comparison. Thus the third square commutes, after the tensor/pullback identification of $T_XQ$ with the changed $Q$. The adjunctions are exactly those stipulated in [fix-prop-adjunctions], not ambient adjunctions on a larger domain.

source.place: Step 1 and final coefficient-comparison and field-stage sentences; explicit transposition and scalar-localization calculation

proof.text:
Let $U=FM\otimes L$, $V=F(M\otimes PL)$, and denote their coefficient comparisons by $d_U:T_YU\to U'$ and $d_V:T_YV\to V'$. Compatibility of the specified projection in [fix-prop-projection-formula] gives
$$d_V\circ T_Y(\operatorname{PF})=\operatorname{PF}'\circ d_U.$$
In the coordinates of step 4, $w'=T_Y(w)\circ d_V^{-1}$, so
$$w'\circ\operatorname{PF}'=T_Y(w\circ\operatorname{PF})\circ d_U^{-1}.$$
This proves the fourth square in the direction required here: precomposition by PF. For the fifth arrow, apply the evaluation-transpose formula [lem-coef-evaluation-transpose-coherence] to $FM$ and $N$ on $Y$, as in step 3 but in the inverse direction. Since the tensor-Hom bijection is injective, equality of the two uncurried maps is equality of their curried maps. Composing the five squares now yields
$$\alpha_B\circ T_Y(\Gamma(u))=\Gamma'(\alpha_A\circ T_Yu).$$
The endpoint comparisons obtained by composing the operation comparisons are precisely $\alpha_A,\alpha_B$ in the statement.

proof.text:
For two successive changes $T,U$, paste the five squares. Tensor reassociation on coefficient complexes is $((x\otimes b)\otimes c)\mapsto x\otimes bc$; its two iterates coincide by associativity of coefficient multiplication. For completed integral scalar extension the compatibility with those same associators is [lem-fix-scalar-completion-associator]; pullback, tensor and Hom comparisons have their tower compatibility in [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension]. The compact-support comparisons respect successive quotient reductions by [lem-fix-compact-support-coefficient-change]; the integral transition and scalar cocycles are part of the supplied other-stage comparison data in [def-exchange-projection]. Ordinary and exceptional right-adjoint comparisons are the specified mates, so their cocycles and identity laws follow from the pasting and identity clauses of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting]. Internal-Hom comparisons satisfy the composite and identity equations of [lem-coef-evaluation-transpose-coherence]. Hence, in the canonical composite coordinates, $\alpha_A^{UT}=\alpha_A^U\circ U(\alpha_A^T)$ and likewise for $B$. Substitution gives
$$\alpha_B^U U(\alpha_B^T)UT(\Gamma u)=\Gamma''\bigl(\alpha_A^U U(\alpha_A^T)UTu\bigr).$$
This is the direct-change equation with exactly its specified comparisons. For integral reduction followed by finite reduction, the quotient reassociation and retained integral transition identifications give the same argument.

proof.text: Implemented localization route: test-object naturality in [lem-pod-hom-chain-counit-formula], applied to an arrow followed by the identity, identifies integralHomEquiv with postcomposition by integralGammaIso.hom from [def-sf-coefficient-gamma-representatives]. The representing isomorphism and Mathlib Linear.homCongr give integral linearity directly, avoiding an additional direct-sum argument. LinearEquiv.baseChange gives the scalar-localized and E-linear equivalences, with its defining pure-tensor formula. A generic tensor induction using ScalarLocalization.composition_tmul shows that base change of postcomposition is postcomposition with the localized representative. Apply this to the forward map and its inverse; functoriality preserves the two inverse equations. Expanding rationalGamma as Iso.homCongr and applying the same composition_tmul identity proves rationalGamma_formula. The integral, rational and common representatives used here are the existing constructions, not new data. The remaining naturality, coefficient and signed-shift transport assertions are still separate unfinished theorems of this module; the following is their retained plan. Integral equalities pass to fractions by bilinearity; [lem-pur-semilinear-scalar-localization] handles equations of natural transformations with semilinear coefficient changes. For E contained in F the image of the uniformizer is invertible, so the coefficient square holds on localized arrows.

proof.text: For algebraically closed coefficients, choose a common finite coefficient field $F$ for all finitely many input objects and arrow representatives. Such stages and the equality criterion are the definition [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. Define $\Gamma([F,u])=[F,\Gamma_F(u)]$, using the operation comparisons for its endpoints. Step 7 localizes the integral scalar-extension square of step 5, so extension from $F$ to a larger $G$ changes $\Gamma_F(u)$ into $\Gamma_G(u_G)$ with exactly the specified endpoint identifications. If two representatives agree over some further field, their images therefore agree there too; this proves independence of both stage and representative. The same construction using $\Gamma_F^{-1}$ is inverse, since both composites are identity at a common field. For representing $a,b$, taking their classes preserves $ab=1$ and $ba=1$ and the postcomposition formulas. Finally every naturality, composition, coefficient-comparison or shift equation involves finitely many arrows: choose one field for all of them, apply the rational equation there, and take its class. The operations on these classes are exactly the induced operations of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom].
